For fuzz_ndpi_reader: seeds include capwap.pcap; mutating a control packet (sport=5246, payload[0]=0x00, offset-13 path) to have a short payload requires: keep eth+ip+udp headers valid, set iph->tot_len small (e.g., 29), and caplen == 14 + tot_len exactly. Mutations that shrink incl_len and fix tot_len... The original capwap.pcap control packet: let me look at it — sport=5246, dport=0x305b=12379, udp len 0x0049=73, ip tot_len 0x005d=93, caplen 0x6b=107 (14+93). To crash: need payload_packet_len < 15 with payload[0] ∈ {0,1} and buffer ending at payload end.

A mutation could zero out iph->tot_len (2 bytes) → len = l3_len = ipsize = caplen - 14 = 93 → payload_packet_len = 93-20-8 = 65 → not < 15. Hmm.

Or mutate incl_len to truncate the packet to e.g. 43 bytes AND fix tot_len to 29. Two coordinated changes — harder but libFuzzer does multi-byte mutations.

Alternatively mutate the IP header's tot_len to 29 (0x001d) while caplen stays 107: then payload_packet_len = 1, payload at offset 42, buffer is 107 bytes → payload[13] = offset 55 < 107 → NO ASAN crash (in-bounds of the malloc'd buffer). Interesting! So for fuzz_ndpi_reader, tot_len mutation alone doesn't crash — the buffer must end exactly at the payload end.

Hmm wait, unless... the reader passes ipsize = caplen - ip_offset = 93, and tot_len=29 < ipsize → valid. payload_packet_len = 29-28 = 1. payload = packet_checked + 14+20+8 = 42. Buffer size 107. payload[13] → offset 55 → in bounds → no crash. Right.

So for fuzz_ndpi_reader the crash needs caplen == 14 + tot_len AND tot_len - 28 < 15. E.g., truncate the packet record (incl_len) to 43 and set tot_len=29. libFuzzer's mutations do include "shrink" operations that reduce the size of the input — when it shrinks the pcap file, it cuts trailing bytes of the file... but the packet data is in the middle... Actually for a single-packet pcap, cutting the file tail reduces incl_len? No — incl_len is stored in the packet header before the data; cutting the file tail just makes the pcap truncated (pcap_next_ex would fail/error on incomplete record). Hmm, actually libpcap: if the record header says incl_len=107 but only e.g. 43 bytes remain in the file, pcap_next_ex returns -2 (EOF) or error → the packet is dropped entirely. So truncation alone doesn't produce a short caplen.

To get caplen=43 with valid data, the fuzzer must change incl_len AND orig_len fields (or craft). Possible via mutation of the 16 bytes at offset 24.

Hmm OK. Both are plausible; fuzz_process_packet actually seems EASIER to reach this crash: it just needs a 29-byte input with the right fields — no pcap structure needed. libFuzzer starting from scratch: build a valid IPv4+UDP packet — the iph->tot_len must equal input size (or 0). Note: tot_len == 0 → len = l3_len → works regardless of size! That's an easy path: any input with 0x45 at byte 0, proto 17 at byte 9, then UDP header with dport 5246 and payload[0] = 0, with tot_len = 0 → l4len = size - 20; payload_packet_len = size - 28. For OOB need size - 28 < 15 → size < 43. And payload must be at the end (always true). So a small input like: 45 00 00 00 ... 40 11 ... udp(dport 5246) + "00" — quite findable.

Honestly, I think fuzz_process_packet might be the more likely finder for this particular bug. But fuzz_ndpi_reader with capwap.pcap seeds is also very plausible...
